title: Configuration
text: Configuration Site-wide options live in an optional staticpedia.json file at the wiki root. Every key is optional: leave the file out entirely and the built-in defaults apply. Unknown keys are ignored. If the file isn't valid JSON, a warning goes to the browser console and the defaults are used. Example This is the configuration of the manual you are reading: { "siteName": "Static-Pedia", "tagline": "The single-file wiki engine", "logo": "images/logo.svg", "favicon": "images/logo.svg", "lang": "en", "defaultTheme": "system", "defaults": { "fontSize": "medium", "width": "narrow", "toc": true, "sidebar": true }, "tocMinHeadings": 3, "showSourceLink": true, "showLastModified": true, "iframeHosts": ["www.youtube-nocookie.com"], "searchExclude": ["README.md", "CLAUDE.md"] } All keys Paths are always relative to the wiki root. Key Default Description siteName "Static-Pedia" Shown in the header and appended to every browser tab title. tagline "" Small line under the site name (hidden on phones). logo "" Image shown left of the site name, e.g. "images/logo.svg". About 40 px tall. favicon built-in icon Browser tab icon, e.g. "images/logo.svg" or "favicon.png". lang "en" (from index.html) The lang attribute of the page, e.g. "de". Helps screen readers and hyphenation. defaultTheme "system" "system", "light" or "dark". Shortcut for defaults.theme. defaults {} Default values for the settings panel: theme, fontSize (small, medium, large, xlarge), width (narrow, wide), toc and sidebar (true/false). Readers' own choices override them. titleSeparator " — " Text between the page title and the site name in the tab title. tocMinHeadings 3 Pages with at least this many section headings get a table of contents. showSourceLink true Show a "View source" link to the page's .md file under each article. showLastModified true Show "This page was last edited on …" when the server sends a Last-Modified header. iframeHosts [] Host names allowed in <iframe src>. See embedding iframes. stylesheets [] Extra CSS files to load after style.css, e.g. ["css/print.css"]. themeStylesheets {} CSS files loaded only for one theme: { "light": "theme-light.css", "dark": "theme-dark.css" }. See Theming. footerText "Powered by Static-Pedia." Footer text used when there is no _Footer.md. "" hides it. searchExclude [] Read only by the search index generator: glob patterns of files to leave out, like "Drafts/**". When configuration is applied staticpedia.json is fetched once per visit, in parallel with the first page. Changing it takes effect on the next page load. Site defaults for settings (defaultTheme and defaults) are also remembered in the reader's browser, so the next visit applies them before the first paint with no flash of the wrong theme. On the very first visit a reader may briefly see the system theme before a different defaultTheme kicks in. Things that are not configurable Some behaviour is fixed so that every Static-Pedia wiki works the same way: The home page is always Index.md, and pages are always addressed with ?p=. The special file names (_Sidebar.md, _Footer.md, style.css, pages.json, staticpedia.json) cannot be renamed. The settings storage key is always staticpedia:settings (see Settings).

title: Examples
text: Examples These pages show what Static-Pedia renders and how the files are laid out. They live in the Examples/ folder of the repository, and this page is Examples/Index.md, which is what a link to Examples/ opens. The people described here are fictional. They exist only to fill sample articles. Page Demonstrates John Doe An encyclopedia article: infobox, hatnote, footnotes, contents box, page-relative images Jane Doe A second article in the same folder, linked both ways, with a floating figure People A folder index page (People/Index.md) Tables Markdown tables, alignment, wide tables on phones, HTML tables with spans Images and media Images, figures, <picture>, video, audio, links to files Markdown showcase Every supported Markdown feature on one page Wiki links [[Page]] links, labels, anchors, and what a missing page looks like The files behind these pages Examples/ ├── Index.md ← this page (?p=Examples/) ├── Tables.md ├── Images_and_Media.md ├── Markdown_Showcase.md ├── Wiki_Links.md ├── files/ │ └── elements.csv ← linked from Images_and_Media.md ├── media/ │ ├── chime.wav │ ├── test-pattern.mp4 │ ├── test-pattern.webm │ └── test-pattern-poster.jpg └── People/ ├── Index.md ← ?p=Examples/People/ ├── John_Doe.md ├── Jane_Doe.md └── images/ ├── john-doe.svg ← written as images/john-doe.svg inside John_Doe.md └── jane-doe.svg Each page links to its neighbours with plain relative links like [Tables](Tables) and [John Doe](People/John_Doe), and back up with ../Index.md. Open any page and use View source at the bottom to compare the Markdown with the result.

title: Markdown showcase
text: Markdown showcase Every Markdown feature Static-Pedia supports, rendered. Use View source at the bottom to see the Markdown behind each example. Text Plain paragraphs are separated by blank lines. Inline styles: italic, also italic, bold, also bold, bold italic, strikethrough, inline code, and Ctrl + C with HTML. Underscores inside words like snake_case_names stay as they are. A line ending in two spaces or a backslash makes a hard line break. Characters with meaning can be escaped: *not italic*, [not a link], `not code`. HTML entities work: © — → ☃. So do inline highlighted , sub script, super script and HTML abbreviations. Headings Heading 1 Heading 2 Heading 3 Heading 4 Heading 5 Heading 6 Setext heading (These sample headings sit inside <div class="no-toc">, which keeps them out of the contents box.) Every heading gets an anchor id: this section is #headings. Hover over a heading to see its # link. Links Relative page link: Installation With .md: Installation To a heading on another page: Wiki links in the manual To a heading on this page: Footnotes Wiki link: Installation, with a label: some tables External: example.com Autolinks: https://example.com, https://www.example.org/path?q=1 and www.example.net E-mail: someone@example.com Reference style: the CommonMark spec and [GFM] Lists Bullets with -, * or + Nested by indenting Second level Third level Back to the first level Numbered Lists Nested numbers Work too Third A list can start at any number Like this one A loose list has blank lines between items. Each item is then a paragraph, and an item can hold several paragraphs, code and more: code inside a list item Task lists Write index.html Write the manual Take over the world Quotes and callouts Block quotes start with >. They can be nested, and contain Markdown, lists and code. GitHub-style callouts: > [!NOTE], > [!TIP], > [!IMPORTANT], > [!WARNING] and > [!CAUTION]. Helpful advice. Key information. Urgent information. Risks and negative outcomes. Code Fenced code blocks with a language name get a language-… class, ready for a highlighter added in style.css or a site script: // index.html renders this page function greet(name) { return `Hello, ${name}!`; } def greet(name): return f"Hello, {name}!" Indented by four spaces: also a code block. Tables Left Center Right a b c 1 2 3 More on the Tables page. Horizontal rules Three dashes, asterisks or underscores: Images The Static-Pedia logo More on Images and media. Collapsible sections Click to expand Hidden content, with Markdown inside because of the blank lines around it. Definition lists (HTML) Static Served as plain files, with no code running on the server. Pedia From encyclopedia . Footnotes Footnotes are written like this. They can have any label, are numbered in the order they are used, and are collected at the bottom of the page with links back. The first footnote. A footnote with a word label. Indented lines continue it. Sanitized HTML The paragraph below contains a <script>, an onclick handler and a javascript: link. All three were removed before the page was shown, so nothing happens: Click me: nothing happens. This link goes nowhere.

title: Jane Doe
text: Jane Doe Jane Doe (born 1972) is a fictional surveyor and the inventor of the Doe projection. She is married to the cartographer John Doe. Doe during a field survey (placeholder image, images/jane-doe.svg ). Early life Jane Doe was born in the inland town of Hollow Reach and spent her childhood measuring things that did not need measuring: the height of the church steeple, the width of the river in flood, the distance to the horizon. The Doe projection The Doe projection is a map projection that preserves the reader's patience at the expense of area, shape and distance. It is used in every map in her husband's atlas. Property Preserved? Area ✗ Shape ✗ Distance ✗ Patience ✓ Field work Choose a coastline. Walk it. Write down everything. Tides Rocks Unusually opinionated seabirds Walk it again, in case it changed. See also John Doe People index Back to Examples

title: John Doe (cartographer)
text: John Doe This article is about the fictional cartographer. For the placeholder name, see John Doe on Wikipedia . John Doe Doe in 1998 (placeholder) Born John Quincy Doe 3 March 1970 Port Ellery, Meridia Occupation Cartographer, surveyor Years active 1991–present Notable work Atlas of Coasts That Never Were (2004) Spouse Jane Doe John Quincy Doe (born 3 March 1970) is a fictional cartographer known for meticulous maps of coastlines that do not exist. He and his wife, the surveyor Jane Doe, are the sample subjects of the Static-Pedia manual. This article is an example page. It shows an infobox built from an HTML table, a hatnote, a table of contents generated from its headings, footnotes, and an image in a sub-folder next to the page (images/john-doe.svg, resolved relative to Examples/People/). Early life Doe grew up in the harbour town of Port Ellery, where his father kept the tide tables. He drew his first map, of the family garden, at the age of seven. It is still considered "ambitious in scale". Career Surveying After studying geodesy, Doe joined the Meridian Survey Office in 1991. There he met Jane Doe, whose projection he later used for all of his published work. The atlas His best-known work, the Atlas of Coasts That Never Were (2004), collects 112 maps drawn to survey standards for places that exist only on paper. Reviewers praised its consistency. Every invented river flows downhill. Edition Year Maps First 2004 112 Revised 2011 130 Pocket 2016 64 Legacy A map is a promise that someone has looked carefully. — John Doe, Atlas, preface Doe's methods are taught in courses on Writing pages (as an example) and nowhere else. See also Jane Doe People (the folder index) More tables (a wiki link, resolved from the wiki root) All examples Notes Neither John nor Jane Doe is a real person. Any resemblance to actual cartographers is coincidental. According to the preface of the Atlas.

title: FAQ and limitations
text: FAQ and limitations Troubleshooting Why does opening index.html from disk not work? Browsers don't let a page opened from a file:// address read other files with fetch(). That is a security rule, and Static-Pedia needs to fetch your .md files. Static-Pedia detects this case and shows instructions. Run any local web server in the wiki folder instead: python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/. Installation lists other one-line servers. Every page says "Page not found" Check the file name, including upper/lower case. Most servers treat People.md and people.md as different files. On GitHub Pages, add an empty .nojekyll file. Without it, Markdown files with front matter are converted to HTML and are no longer available as .md. See GitHub Pages. Make sure the address ends in / when the wiki lives in a folder (/wiki/, not /wiki). See the trailing-slash note. The sidebar or footer is missing on GitHub Pages Same cause: Jekyll doesn't publish files starting with _. Add .nojekyll. My images or links are broken Relative paths are resolved from the folder of the page they appear in, not from the wiki root. In People/John_Doe.md, images/a.png means People/images/a.png. Use ../images/a.png or /images/a.png (where a leading / means the wiki root) for files at the root. See Links and media. A link to Version_2.0 opens a file instead of a page Links with a file extension are treated as files. .0 has no letters, so Version_2.0 is still a page, but Release.notes would be a file. Add .md to be explicit: [notes](Release.notes.md). I changed a page but still see the old version Static-Pedia asks the server to revalidate each page (cache: no-cache), so edits normally show up on the next click. A CDN in front of your host may still cache files for a while. style.css and staticpedia.json follow your host's normal caching rules; a hard refresh ( Ctrl / Cmd + Shift + R ) helps. Search doesn't find my new page Regenerate pages.json with node tools/build-index.mjs. See Search. Limitations These are deliberate. They keep Static-Pedia a single file that runs on any static host. No editing in the browser. Static-Pedia is read-only. Edit the Markdown files with any editor and upload them, or use GitHub's web editor and pull requests. No server-side rendering. Pages are built in the reader's browser with JavaScript. Without JavaScript, readers see a short notice. Search engines that run JavaScript, like Google, can index the pages; ones that don't only see the empty shell. No file://. A web server is always needed, even locally. No automatic page list. Static hosts don't provide directory listings, so Static-Pedia can't discover pages by itself. Navigation comes from your links, _Sidebar.md, and the optional pages.json. No red links by default. Static-Pedia can't cheaply check whether a linked page exists, so links to missing pages look like normal links and lead to the "page not found" page. You can mark them by hand with class="new". Fixed home page and addresses. The home page is always Index.md, and pages always use ?p=. Pretty URLs like /wiki/People/John_Doe would need server rewrites. Simple front matter. Only one-line key: value pairs are read. Markdown inside HTML blocks is only processed when separated from the tags by blank lines, as in CommonMark. Embedded content (

title: GitHub Pages
text: GitHub Pages GitHub Pages is the easiest free home for a Static-Pedia wiki. Your Markdown lives in a repository, people can propose edits with pull requests, and every push republishes the site. This manual is published exactly this way. Publish from a branch Create a repository, or use an existing one, and add index.html, Index.md and your other pages. Add an empty file called .nojekyll at the root of what you publish (see below). Push to GitHub. In the repository, open Settings → Pages. Under Build and deployment, choose Source: Deploy from a branch, pick your branch (for example master or main) and the folder (/ (root) or /docs), and click Save. After a minute the site is live at https://<user>.github.io/<repository>/. The address has a sub-path (/<repository>/), which Static-Pedia handles without any configuration. With a custom domain the same files are served from the root instead. Nothing changes on your side. Keeping the wiki in a sub-folder If the repository also contains other things, put the wiki in docs/ and choose /docs as the publishing folder. Only that folder is published, so index.html, .nojekyll and the pages all go inside docs/. Why .nojekyll matters By default GitHub Pages runs every site through Jekyll. For a Static-Pedia wiki that causes two problems: Jekyll does not publish files or folders whose names start with _, so _Sidebar.md and _Footer.md disappear. Jekyll converts Markdown files that have front matter into HTML, so ?p= can no longer fetch the raw .md and you get "page not found". An empty .nojekyll file at the published root turns Jekyll off and the files are served exactly as committed: touch .nojekyll git add .nojekyll git commit -m "Serve files as-is on GitHub Pages" Building the search index automatically The search box appears when the site has a pages.json file. You can regenerate it on every push with GitHub Actions instead of remembering to run the generator yourself. Option A: commit pages.json back to the branch This keeps "Deploy from a branch" publishing. Save as .github/workflows/search-index.yml: name: Update search index on: push: branches: [master] paths: ['**.md', 'staticpedia.json'] workflow_dispatch: permissions: contents: write jobs: index: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 - run: node tools/build-index.mjs - name: Commit pages.json if it changed run: | if ! git diff --quiet -- pages.json; then git config user.name "github-actions[bot]" git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" git add pages.json git commit -m "Update search index" git push fi The paths filter means the workflow's own commit (which changes only pages.json) does not trigger it again. Option B: build during deployment If you publish with Source: GitHub Actions, generate the index in the deploy job and never commit it: name: Deploy wiki on: push: branches: [master] workflow_dispatch: permissions: contents: read pages: write id-token: write concurrency: group: pages cancel-in-progress: true jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest environment: name: github-pages url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 - run: node tools/build-index.mjs - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5 - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 with: path: . - id: deployment uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4 Artifacts uploaded this way are not processed by Jekyll, but keeping .nojekyll does no harm. To make a pull request fail when someone forgets to rebuild the index, run node tools/build-index.mjs --check in CI. It exits with an error if pages.json is out of date and changes nothing. Editing on GitHub Because pages are ordinary Markdown files, GitHub's web editor and pull requests work as your wiki's editing workflow. GitHub's own Markdown preview is close to what Static-Pedia renders. The differences are the [[wiki link]] syntax and the link rules (GitHub's preview does not rewrite ?p= links).

title: Static-Pedia
text: Welcome to Static-Pedia Static-Pedia is a read-only, wiki-style encyclopedia engine delivered as one self-contained index.html file. Put it at the top of a folder of Markdown files, upload the folder to any static web host, and the files become a browsable wiki. You get a sidebar, search, a table of contents on every long page, and light and dark themes. This site is Static-Pedia. Every page you are reading is a plain .md file in the repository, rendered in your browser by index.html. It doubles as the reference manual: start with Installation or pick a topic from the sidebar. One file The whole program (parser, sanitizer, styles, icons) lives in index.html . No CDN, no fonts fetched from third parties, no build step. Any static host GitHub Pages, python -m http.server , nginx, S3, Netlify. Works at the domain root or under a sub-path like /wiki/ . Plain Markdown GitHub-flavored Markdown with tables, task lists, footnotes, wiki links and sanitized HTML for infoboxes. Yours to restyle Every color and font is a CSS variable. Drop a style.css next to index.html to override them. Quick start Download index.html from this site, or grab it from the repository. Put it in the folder that holds your Markdown, next to a file called Index.md. That file is your home page. Serve the folder with any web server, for example: cd my-wiki python3 -m http.server 8000 Open http://localhost:8000/. A link to ?p=People/John_Doe shows People/John_Doe.md. A typical wiki looks like this: my-wiki/ ├── index.html ← Static-Pedia (the only program file) ├── Index.md ← home page → /my-wiki/ ├── _Sidebar.md ← optional navigation panel ├── People.md ← a page → ?p=People └── People/ ├── John_Doe.md ← a page in a folder → ?p=People/John_Doe └── images/ └── portrait.png You can't open index.html by double-clicking it. Browsers block the requests it needs on file:// URLs, so you always need a web server, even a local one. See FAQ. How it works Diagram: the browser opens /wiki/?p=People/Ada, index.html fetches /wiki/People/Ada.md and renders it as a wiki page When someone visits ?p=People/Ada, index.html fetches People/Ada.md from the same folder it was loaded from. It converts the Markdown to HTML, removes anything unsafe, rewrites relative links and images so they point at the right files, and shows the result. Clicking another wiki link swaps the page in place without a full reload, and the browser's Back and Forward buttons work as usual. What's in this manual Page What it covers Installation Installing at the root or a sub-path, local preview, hosting options GitHub Pages Publishing a wiki from a GitHub repository, step by step Writing pages File names, titles, front matter, Markdown syntax, raw HTML Links and media Page links, wiki links, anchors, images, video, audio, files Special files _Sidebar.md, _Footer.md, style.css, pages.json, staticpedia.json Configuration Every option in staticpedia.json Theming CSS variables, dark mode, style.css, content classes Settings panel The gear menu, what readers can change, how it is stored Search The search box, pages.json, the generator script, GitHub Actions FAQ and limitations Troubleshooting and the things Static-Pedia deliberately does not do Instructions for AI agents A compact, rule-by-rule guide for AI coding agents that install Static-Pedia and write wikis The Examples section shows what the renderer can do: an article with an infobox, tables, images and media, and a tour of the Markdown syntax. Screenshots An article in the light theme. The same page in the dark theme. Readers pick a theme from the gear menu.

title: Installation
text: Installation Installing Static-Pedia means copying one file, index.html, into the folder that holds your Markdown. Nothing is compiled or configured on the server. This page covers getting the file, installing it at the root of a site or under a sub-path, previewing it on your own computer, and the hosting services known to work. What you need index.html from the Static-Pedia repository. It is the only program file. A folder of Markdown files with an Index.md home page. Any host that serves static files over HTTP or HTTPS. No PHP, Node, rewrites or directory listings are required. Readers need a current browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari from the last few years. Static-Pedia uses modern JavaScript (ES2020) and the <dialog> element. Everything else is optional: a _Sidebar.md navigation panel, a style.css, a staticpedia.json config file and a pages.json search index. Installing at the root of a site Put index.html and Index.md at the top level of what your host publishes: public/ ├── index.html ├── Index.md └── Guides/ └── Getting_Started.md Then: Address Shows https://example.com/ Index.md https://example.com/?p=Guides/Getting_Started Guides/Getting_Started.md https://example.com/?p=Guides/Getting_Started.md the same page (the .md is optional) https://example.com/?p=Guides/ Guides/Index.md Installing under a sub-path Static-Pedia never assumes it lives at /. It works out its own folder from the page address and loads every file relative to that folder. You can install it as deep as you like: example.com/ ├── index.html ← your normal website └── docs/ └── wiki/ ├── index.html ← Static-Pedia ├── Index.md └── People/John_Doe.md Here https://example.com/docs/wiki/?p=People/John_Doe loads https://example.com/docs/wiki/People/John_Doe.md, and an image written as ![](images/a.png) inside that page loads /docs/wiki/People/images/a.png. Because of this you can move a whole wiki folder to a different path or host without changing a single link, as long as your pages use relative links (see Links and media). Keep the trailing slash. Link to https://example.com/docs/wiki/, not .../docs/wiki. Most hosts (GitHub Pages, nginx, Apache, Netlify, python -m http.server) redirect the short form for you. If yours does not, the browser treats wiki as a file name and relative URLs resolve one folder too high. Linking to .../wiki/index.html explicitly also works. Previewing on your own computer Browsers refuse to let a page loaded from file:// fetch other files, so double-clicking index.html cannot work. Start a tiny local web server in the wiki folder instead. Any of these will do: # Python 3 (preinstalled on macOS and most Linux distributions) python3 -m http.server 8000 # Node.js npx http-server -p 8000 npx serve . # PHP php -S localhost:8000 Then open http://localhost:8000/. To check that your wiki also works under a sub-path, start the server in the parent folder and visit the wiki's folder name: cd .. # the folder that contains my-wiki/ python3 -m http.server 8000 # now open http://localhost:8000/my-wiki/ npx serve with its --single (SPA) flag, and other servers that answer every unknown URL with index.html, still work. Static-Pedia notices when it gets an HTML page back instead of Markdown and shows its "page not found" message. Hosting options Static-Pedia only needs a host that serves files as they are. These are known to work: Host Notes GitHub Pages Add an empty .nojekyll file, or GitHub's Jekyll step hides _Sidebar.md and _Footer.md and converts Markdown files that have front matter. See GitHub Pages. GitLab Pages, Codeberg Pages Publish the folder as-is. Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel Use "no build command" and publish the wiki folder. SPA fallback rules are fine but not needed. Amazon S3 (+ CloudFront) Set index.html as the index document. S3 answers missing files with 403 when the bucket isn't listable; Static-Pedia treats that as "page not found". nginx, Apache, Caddy, IIS Serve the folder as static files. No rewrite rules are needed. Any shared web hosting Upload with FTP/SFTP like any other files. nginx The default configuration works. Optionally give Markdown a proper content type and stop browsers caching stale pages for too long: location /wiki/ { index index.html; types { text/markdown md; text/html html; text/css css; application/json json; image/svg+xml svg; } add_header Cache-Control "no-cache"; } Apache Works out of the box. To serve Markdown as UTF-8 text, add this to .htaccess: AddType "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" .md Upgrading Replace index.html with the new version. Your pages, style.css and staticpedia.json are untouched, and the public conventions (special file names, ?p= addresses, CSS variables) are kept stable between versions. Checklist index.html and Index.md are in the same folder The folder is served over http:// or https://, not opened from disk Links to the wiki end in / Optional: _Sidebar.md for navigation (Special files) Optional: staticpedia.json with your site name and logo (Configuration) Optional: pages.json for search (Search) GitHub Pages only: an empty .nojekyll file (GitHub Pages)

title: Links and media
text: Links and media Static-Pedia rewrites every link and media URL in a page so it works wherever the wiki is installed, whether that is the root of a domain or /some/deep/sub-path/. This page explains the rules. Links to other pages Write ordinary Markdown links with paths relative to the current page's folder. The .md extension is optional: Written in People/John_Doe.md Goes to [Jane](Jane_Doe) People/Jane_Doe.md [Jane](Jane_Doe.md) People/Jane_Doe.md [Jane](./Jane_Doe.md) People/Jane_Doe.md [Home](../Index.md) Index.md [Tables](../Examples/Tables) Examples/Tables.md [Everyone](./) People/Index.md [Install](/Installation) Installation.md: a leading / means the wiki root, not the host root [Early life](Jane_Doe#early-life) People/Jane_Doe.md, scrolled to that heading [See below](#references) a heading on the same page Each of these becomes a ?p=... link. Clicking it swaps the page in place without reloading, and Back/Forward work normally. Opening it in a new tab or sharing it also works, because the address is a real URL. Writing the links this way keeps your Markdown readable on GitHub and in editors, which understand relative .md links too. Page or file? A relative link is treated as a page when it ends in .md, ends in /, or has no file extension. Anything with another extension (report.pdf, data.csv, photo.jpg) is treated as a file and linked directly, relative to the page's folder. A page name that contains a dot, like Version_2.0, still counts as a page because .0 has no letters. If in doubt, add .md. Links with query strings Links starting with ? are passed through, so you can link to built-in pages: Link Shows [All pages](?special=AllPages) every page in the search index, grouped by folder [Random page](?special=Random) a random page from the search index [Search for cats](?search=cats) search results The special pages need pages.json. Wiki links Double square brackets link to a page by name, the way MediaWiki and GitHub wikis do: You write Goes to Shows [[Installation]] Installation.md Installation [[Writing Pages]] Writing_Pages.md Writing Pages [[Examples/People/John_Doe|John]] Examples/People/John_Doe.md John [[Theming#CSS variables]] Theming.md at #css-variables Theming#CSS variables [[#Wiki links]] this page's "Wiki links" heading #Wiki links Spaces become underscores. Unlike relative Markdown links, wiki link targets are always resolved from the wiki root, so [[People/John_Doe]] means the same thing on every page. The text after is the label. Inside a table, write the bar as | so it doesn't split the cell. See them in action on Wiki links. External links Links with a scheme (https://, http://, mailto:, tel:…) or starting with // open normally. They get rel="noopener" and a small arrow icon so readers can tell they are leaving the wiki: example.com. Bare URLs such as https://example.com and become links automatically. To open a link in a new tab, use HTML: . Static-Pedia adds rel="noopener noreferrer". Images Image paths are relative to the page's folder too: ![The Static-Pedia logo](images/logo.svg "Optional title") The Static-Pedia logo Written in People/John_Doe.md, ![](images/portrait.svg) loads People/images/portrait.svg, and ![](/images/logo.svg) loads images/logo.svg from the wiki root. Images are never wider than the text column and load lazily. For sizes, captions and floating, use HTML: , srcset and sizes work too, and every URL in them is rewritten the same way. Video and audio Use the HTML elements directly. src, poster and the src of every and are resolved relative to the page: Images and media shows working examples. Links to files Link to PDFs, spreadsheets, archives or anything else like any other relative link: [Download the data (CSV)](files/elements.csv) The browser opens or downloads the file itself. Add download in HTML () to force a download. Embedding iframes Only https:// URLs whose host exactly matches an entry are kept. Static-Pedia always adds a sandbox attribute, lazy loading and a strict referrer policy, and drops every other attribute except width, height, title, class and style. Embeds load content from another site, so they don't work on an offline or air-gapped wiki and they let that site see who reads the page. Allow only hosts you trust. Checking links tools/check-links.mjs finds broken page links, wiki links, images, media, file links and #anchors without a browser. It resolves them with exactly the rules on this page: node tools/check-links.mjs # or: node tools/check-links.mjs path/to/wiki Guides/Setup.md:12: broken page link "Instal" -> Guides/Instal.md does not exist Guides/Setup.md:20: missing anchor "#frist-run" in Guides/Setup.md (did you mean #first-run?) It exits with status 1 when anything is broken, so it can run in CI next to build-index.mjs --check. External links, code, red links and lines containing `` are skipped.

title: Search
text: Search Static-Pedia has no server to run searches on, so it searches a manifest file, pages.json, that lists every page with its title and text. When pages.json exists at the wiki root, a search box appears in the header. Without it the search box stays hidden and everything else works as normal. Using search Type in the search box (or press / to jump to it). Up to eight matching pages appear as you type, best first. ↑ and ↓ move through the suggestions, Enter opens the highlighted one, and Esc closes the list. Enter with nothing highlighted, or Search all pages for…, opens the full results page with a text snippet for each match. Its address is ?search=your+words, so searches can be bookmarked and shared, for example ?search=sidebar. Every word must appear in a page's title, path or text. Matching ignores case and accents ("cafe" finds "Café"). Pages whose title matches rank first, then pages that mention the words most often. The manifest also powers two special pages: All pages (?special=AllPages), a list of every page grouped by folder, and Random page (?special=Random). "Page not found" pages suggest similarly named pages too. The pages.json format A JSON array with one object per page: [ { "path": "People/John_Doe", "title": "John Doe", "text": "John Doe (born 1970) is a fictional cartographer…" } ] Field Required Meaning path yes The page's path as used in ?p=, without .md (a trailing .md is tolerated). title no Display title. Defaults to the file name with underscores as spaces. text no Plain text to search: an excerpt or the whole page. The file is downloaded once per visit, so keep it reasonable. A few megabytes is fine for most readers; the generator's --max-chars option limits text per page. { "pages": [...] } is accepted as well as a bare array. Generating pages.json The repository includes a small generator with no dependencies. Run it from the wiki root: node tools/build-index.mjs Wrote 19 pages to pages.json It needs Node.js 18 or newer. There is a Python equivalent that produces the same file, for machines without Node: python3 tools/build_index.py The generator walks the folder, reads every .md file and records: path: the file's path without .md. title: the front matter title, else the first # Heading, else the file name. This matches what Static-Pedia shows. text: the page as plain text, with Markdown syntax, HTML tags, front matter and link targets removed, and code blocks kept. It skips files and folders whose names start with . or _ (so _Sidebar.md and _Footer.md are never results), node_modules, and pages with noindex: true in their front matter. Options Option Meaning node tools/build-index.mjs path/to/wiki Index a different folder (pages.json is written inside it). --out FILE Write somewhere else. --max-chars N Keep at most N characters of text per page (default 20000, 0 for no limit). --exclude GLOB Leave out matching files. Repeatable. * matches within a folder, ** across folders: --exclude "Drafts/**" --exclude "*.draft.md". --check Write nothing. Exit with status 1 if pages.json is missing or out of date. Useful in CI. --quiet Print nothing on success. Patterns can also be listed in staticpedia.json under searchExclude, which is how this manual keeps README.md out of its index: { "searchExclude": ["README.md", "CLAUDE.md"] } Keeping the index up to date pages.json is only as fresh as the last time you ran the generator. Common setups: Run it before you commit, or add it to a Git pre-commit hook. Let GitHub Actions do it on every push. GitHub Pages has ready-to-use workflows that either commit pages.json back or build it during deployment. Check it in CI with node tools/build-index.mjs --check. A stale index never breaks the wiki: a page missing from it is just not found by search, and a result for a deleted page leads to the friendly "page not found" page. Without the generator The generator is a convenience. You can write pages.json by hand, produce it from another tool or CMS, or leave it out entirely. Static-Pedia works fully without it; you just don't get the search box and the special pages.

title: Settings panel
text: Settings panel The gear button in the upper-right corner of every page opens a settings panel. Readers use it to adjust the wiki to their taste. Choices take effect immediately and are remembered in their browser. The settings Setting Choices Default Theme System, Light, Dark System: follows the operating system and switches when it does Text size Small, Standard, Large, Extra large Standard Content width Narrow (a comfortable reading measure), Wide (use the whole window) Narrow Show table of contents on / off on Show sidebar on / off on Reset to defaults forgets the reader's choices and goes back to the site's defaults. The site owner can change those defaults with defaultTheme and defaults in staticpedia.json. On wide screens the ☰ button next to the site name toggles Show sidebar too. On phones the sidebar is always a slide-out drawer opened with ☰, whatever the setting says. Keyboard and accessibility The panel is a modal dialog. Focus moves into it when it opens, Tab cycles through its controls without escaping to the page behind, and focus returns to the gear button when it closes. Esc , the Done button, the × button or a click on the dimmed backdrop close it. Theme, text size and width are radio groups (arrow keys move between choices). The other two are checkboxes. Elsewhere on the page, / jumps to the search box and Esc closes the mobile sidebar. Animations are turned off when the reader's system asks for reduced motion. How settings are stored Settings live in localStorage under a single key, staticpedia:settings, as a small JSON object. Only the settings a reader actually changed are saved, so site defaults still apply to the rest: { "theme": "dark", "fontSize": "large", "_site": { "theme": "system", "fontSize": "medium", "width": "narrow", "toc": true, "sidebar": true } } _site is a cached copy of the site's defaults from staticpedia.json. It lets the theme be applied before the page is first drawn, so readers never see a flash of the wrong theme. All storage access is wrapped so that a browser blocking storage (private modes, strict privacy settings, sandboxed iframes) never breaks the wiki. Settings then still work but last only until the reader leaves the page, and the panel says so. Every Static-Pedia wiki on the same origin (for example several wikis under one https://user.github.io/ address) shares the same key, so a reader's preferences follow them between those wikis. Changing a setting in one tab updates other open tabs immediately. Adding your own setting The settings are defined by one schema near the top of index.html, and the panel is generated from it. To add a setting, for example a "Justify text" toggle: Find const SCHEMA = [ in the first <script> in index.html and add an entry: { key: 'justify', label: 'Justify text', type: 'toggle', default: false }, A choice setting looks like this: { key: 'font', label: 'Font', type: 'choice', default: 'sans', options: [['sans', 'Sans-serif'], ['serif', 'Serif']] }, Each setting is written to <html> as a data-* attribute (justify → data-justify="on", fontSize → data-font-size="large"), before the first paint. Style it in style.css: :root[data-justify="on"] .sp-content p { text-align: justify; hyphens: auto; } :root[data-font="serif"] { --sp-font-body: Georgia, serif; } Site owners can then set a default with "defaults": { "justify": true } in staticpedia.json. Scripts can also read and change settings through window.StaticPedia.settings.get('theme'), .set('theme', 'dark') and .open().

title: Special files
text: Special files A few file names at the wiki root (the folder containing index.html) have special meaning. All of them are optional except Index.md, and a missing one is never an error. These names are a stable public convention. File Purpose Index.md Home page, shown when there is no p in the address. _Sidebar.md Rendered as the left navigation panel on every page. _Footer.md Rendered as the footer on every page. style.css Your custom styles, loaded after the built-in defaults so they win. pages.json Search manifest. When it exists, the header shows a search box. staticpedia.json Site configuration: name, logo, default theme and more. .nojekyll Not read by Static-Pedia, but needed on GitHub Pages. Two more files are loaded only if staticpedia.json names them: per-theme stylesheets (themeStylesheets) and extra stylesheets (stylesheets). Index.md The front page of the wiki. Any folder can also have an Index.md, which is shown for ?p=Folder/ and for relative links that end in /, such as [People](People/). _Sidebar.md Ordinary Markdown shown in the navigation panel to the left of every page. Links in it are relative to the wiki root, whichever page is being viewed. The link to the current page is highlighted. If there is no _Sidebar.md, the panel and its menu button are hidden and pages use the full width. A typical sidebar is a few short lists under small headings: - [Main page](Index) - [All pages](?special=AllPages) ### People - [John Doe](People/John_Doe) - [Jane Doe](People/Jane_Doe) ### Places - [[Places/Springfield|Springfield]] Headings in the sidebar are styled as small section labels, and lists have no bullets. On narrow screens the sidebar collapses behind the ☰ menu button. On wide screens the same button hides or shows it (readers can also do that in settings). _Footer.md Markdown shown at the bottom of every page, below the article. It is a good place for a copyright line, a licence or contact details. Links in it are relative to the wiki root. Without a _Footer.md the footer shows the footerText setting ("Powered by Static-Pedia." by default). Set footerText to an empty string to show nothing. style.css Loaded right after Static-Pedia's built-in styles, on every page. It can override any CSS variable or rule. If the file doesn't exist the request fails quietly (your browser's developer console notes a 404) and the default look remains. See Theming. pages.json An optional search manifest: [ { "path": "People/John_Doe", "title": "John Doe", "text": "John Doe is a fictional…" } ] When present, Static-Pedia shows the search box, enables the ?special=AllPages and ?special=Random pages, and suggests similar pages on "not found" pages. Generate it with node tools/build-index.mjs. See Search. staticpedia.json Site-wide settings such as the site name, logo and default theme. All keys are optional, unknown keys are ignored, and invalid JSON is reported in the console and otherwise ignored. See Configuration for every key. Other conventions Files and folders whose names start with _ or . are skipped by the search index generator. Use them for drafts, templates or partials you don't want in search. They can still be opened with ?p=. Folders are just folders. A file in People/ is addressed as ?p=People/Name. There are no special category files.

title: Theming
text: Theming Static-Pedia's built-in look is a clean encyclopedia style with a light and a dark theme. You can change all of it with a style.css file next to index.html. Usually you only need to override a few CSS variables. How styles are loaded In order, each layer overriding the previous ones: Built-in styles inside index.html. style.css at the wiki root, if it exists. Extra stylesheets listed in stylesheets in staticpedia.json. The per-theme stylesheet for the active theme, if themeStylesheets names one (below). Everything must be served from your own site: Static-Pedia never fetches fonts or styles from third parties. If you want a web font, put the font file in your wiki folder and declare it with @font-face in style.css. Light and dark themes The active theme is written on the <html> element before the page is drawn: <html data-theme="dark" data-theme-pref="system"> data-theme is always light or dark. It is the theme actually shown, after resolving "System" against the reader's operating system. data-theme-pref is the reader's choice (system, light or dark). So: /* Applies in both themes */ :root { --sp-accent: #0b7a75; } /* Only in the light theme */ :root[data-theme="light"] { --sp-bg: #fbf8f1; } /* Only in the dark theme */ :root[data-theme="dark"] { --sp-bg: #0d1117; } Built-in dark values are set with :root[data-theme="dark"]. Use at least that specificity to override them; a plain :root rule in style.css applies to both themes but loses to the built-in dark values. CSS variables Colors Variable Used for Light Dark --sp-bg Page background around the article, header, sidebar #f6f6f6 #101418 --sp-surface Article background, dialogs, dropdowns #ffffff #171b20 --sp-surface-2 Infoboxes, contents box, tables, callouts #f8f9fa #1f242a --sp-surface-3 Table headers, hover states #eaecf0 #2a3038 --sp-text Body text #202122 #e8eaed --sp-text-muted Secondary text, captions, footer #54595d #a8b0b9 --sp-border Strong borders (tables, inputs) #a2a9b1 #5b636c --sp-border-light Subtle borders, heading rules #c8ccd1 #343b43 --sp-link Links #3366cc #88a3e8 --sp-link-visited Visited links #6b4ba1 #b9a1ec --sp-link-hover Hovered links #447ff5 #aac0f5 --sp-link-new Links with class new (red links) #d73333 #ff8a80 --sp-accent Buttons, active states, focus #3366cc #6d8fe0 --sp-accent-text Text on accent backgrounds #ffffff #0b0e11 --sp-focus Keyboard focus outline #3366cc #88a3e8 --sp-header-bg Header background var(--sp-bg) --sp-sidebar-bg Sidebar background (desktop) var(--sp-bg) --sp-input-bg Search box background #ffffff #0c0f12 --sp-code-bg, --sp-code-text Inline code and code blocks #f3f4f6, #000 #22272e, #e8eaed --sp-mark-bg Search highlights, targeted footnotes #fef6b5 #5c4f12 --sp-note, --sp-tip, --sp-important, --sp-warning, --sp-caution Callout colors --sp-shadow Dropdown and dialog shadows Typography and layout Variable Default Used for --sp-font-body system UI font stack Body text and interface --sp-font-heading "Linux Libertine", Georgia, …, serif Page title, h1/h2, site name --sp-font-mono ui-monospace, …, monospace Code --sp-font-scale 1 (set by the text-size setting) Scales the root font size --sp-line-height 1.6 Body line height --sp-page-max 100rem Maximum width of the whole layout --sp-sidebar-width 11.5rem Sidebar width on wide screens --sp-content-max 58rem (none in "wide" mode) Maximum width of the article text --sp-radius 4px Corner radius of boxes and inputs Settings hooks Each reader setting is also an attribute on <html>, so you can style around them: Attribute Values data-theme / data-theme-pref see above data-font-size small, medium, large, xlarge data-width narrow, wide data-toc on, off data-sidebar on, off For example, a wider measure in narrow mode: :root[data-width="narrow"] { --sp-content-max: 64rem; } Per-theme stylesheets If your theme customizations are large, keep them in separate files and name them in staticpedia.json: { "themeStylesheets": { "light": "theme-light.css", "dark": "theme-dark.css" } } The matching file is loaded after style.css and swapped whenever the theme changes. Rules in it don't need a [data-theme] selector, but variables still need enough specificity to beat the built-in dark values, so use :root[data-theme] in them. Content classes These classes are styled by default and can be used in raw HTML in any page: Class Element Effect infobox table or div Right-floating summary box. Inside: caption or .infobox-title for the name, th.infobox-header for section rows, td.infobox-image for a centered picture, .infobox-caption for its caption. Full width on phones. thumb figure Framed figure with caption. right, left, center figure Floated (and framed) figure, or a centered one. float-right, float-left any Float without a frame. center any Center the content. clear any Start below all floats. hatnote p, div Indented italic note under a title ("For other uses…"). notice (or ambox) div Boxed message with a colored left edge. plain table No borders or background. new a Red "page doesn't exist yet" link color. no-toc any Headings inside are left out of the contents box. callout callout-note (… tip, important, warning, caution) div Generated by > [!NOTE] and friends. You can write them by hand too. All Markdown tables get the classic "wikitable" look: borders, padding, shaded header cells. Wide tables scroll sideways inside their own box on small screens instead of stretching the page. Interface structure For bigger changes, these are the main parts of the page. All class names start with sp-: .sp-header site name/logo (.sp-brand), search (.sp-search), gear (.sp-gear) .sp-layout nav.sp-sidebar rendered _Sidebar.md (#sp-sidebar-content) .sp-column main.sp-main article.sp-article .sp-content the rendered page .sp-page-info "last edited" and "view source" footer.sp-footer rendered _Footer.md dialog.sp-dialog settings panel Recipes Change the accent color everywhere: :root, :root[data-theme="dark"] { --sp-accent: #0b7a75; --sp-link: #0b7a75; --sp-focus: #0b7a75; } :root[data-theme="dark"] { --sp-link: #5fd3cc; } Use a self-hosted font: @font-face { font-family: "Source Serif"; src: url("fonts/SourceSerif4-Regular.woff2") format("woff2"); font-display: swap; } :root { --sp-font-heading: "Source Serif", Georgia, serif; } A sepia light theme: :root[data-theme="light"] { --sp-bg: #f1e7d0; --sp-surface: #fbf4e4; --sp-surface-2: #f4ead3; --sp-surface-3: #e9dcbd; --sp-text: #3b2f22; --sp-border-light: #d8c7a3; --sp-code-bg: #efe3c8; } Hide the "View source" link with CSS (or set showSourceLink to false): .sp-page-info a[rel="nofollow"] { display: none; } The style.css of this manual is a small working example. View it.

title: Writing pages
text:
Writing pages Every page is a Markdown (.md) file somewhere under the folder that contains index.html. This page explains how file names become addresses and titles, what Markdown is supported, and how raw HTML is handled. Links, images and other media have their own page: Links and media. File names and addresses The page shown is chosen by the p query parameter. Its value is a path relative to the wiki root, with or without .md: Address File loaded index.html (no p) Index.md ?p=People People.md ?p=People/John_Doe People/John_Doe.md ?p=People/John_Doe.md People/John_Doe.md ?p=People/ People/Index.md ?p=People/John Doe People/John_Doe.md (spaces become underscores) ?p=People/John_Doe#early-life People/John_Doe.md, scrolled to the "Early life" heading Conventions that keep a wiki tidy: Use underscores instead of spaces in file names: Jane_Doe.md, not Jane Doe.md. Underscores are shown as spaces in titles that come from file names. Case matters on most hosts. People.md and people.md are different files on Linux servers and GitHub Pages, though not on a Mac or Windows laptop. Pick one style and stick with it. A folder can have its own Index.md, which is what ?p=Folder/ and links to Folder/ show. Names starting with _ are reserved for special files and are skipped by the search index generator. Requests that try to escape the wiki are refused with an "Invalid page name" message: values starting with /, containing .. segments or backslashes, or that look like URLs (http:, javascript: and so on). If the file does not exist, readers get a friendly "Page not found" page with a link back to the main page and, when search is available, suggestions. Page titles The big heading at the top of a page, and the browser tab title, are chosen like this: Heading: the page's first # Heading 1. If the page has no level-1 heading, Static-Pedia adds one from the front matter title, or else from the file name (John_Doe → "John Doe"; a folder's Index.md uses the folder name, and the root Index.md uses the site name). Tab title: front matter title if present, otherwise the first # Heading 1, otherwise the file name, followed by — and the site name. On the page whose title equals the site name (like this manual's home page) the tab shows just the site name. Start most pages with exactly one # Title line and use ## and below for sections, as Wikipedia does. Front matter A page may start with a YAML-style block between --- lines. It is not shown on the page. --- title: John Doe (cartographer) toc: false noindex: true --- # John Doe ... Key Effect title Browser tab title, the heading when the page has no # H1, and the title in search results. toc false hides the table of contents on this page. noindex true keeps the page out of pages.json, so it never appears in search. (Used by the generator only.) Other keys are allowed and ignored, so you can keep your own metadata there. Only simple key: value lines are understood, not nested YAML. Headings, anchors and the table of contents Every heading gets an id so you can link to it. The id is the heading text in lower case, with punctuation removed and spaces turned into dashes: Heading Anchor ## Early life #early-life ## Works (1990–2001) #works-19902001 ### What's new? #whats-new Duplicates get -1, -2 and so on. Hover over a heading to reveal a # link you can copy. Pages with three or more section headings get a Wikipedia-style Contents box just before the first section. Readers can hide it everywhere from the settings panel, you can turn it off for one page with toc: false in the front matter, and the site owner can change the threshold with tocMinHeadings. Headings inside tables, block quotes,
, callouts, infoboxes or any element with class no-toc are left out of the box. Markdown syntax Static-Pedia includes its own parser for CommonMark plus the GitHub extensions people expect. See the Markdown showcase for every feature rendered live. You write You get *italic* or _italic_ italic **bold** bold ~~struck~~ struck `code` code [link](Writing_Pages) link [[Writing Pages]] Writing Pages https://example.com https://example.com ![alt](images/logo.svg) an image - item / 1. item bulleted / numbered lists, nested by indenting - [ ] todo / - [x] done task lists > quote block quote > [!NOTE] a note callout (also TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION) ```js fenced code block (the language becomes a language-js class) --- horizontal rule | a | b | tables, with :--: alignment text[^1] + [^1]: note footnotes, collected at the end of the page Raw HTML You can mix HTML into Markdown, which is how infoboxes, figures with captions and complex tables are built:
Example
Born1 January 1970
A block of HTML ends at the first blank line. Leave a blank line after an opening tag if you want Markdown to be processed inside it:
This **is** Markdown, because of the blank lines around it.
What the sanitizer removes All HTML, whether written by hand or produced from Markdown, passes through a built-in allowlist sanitizer before it reaches the page. That makes it safe to publish pages from many authors: Removed with their content:

title: Static-Pedia: install it, configure it, write the wiki
text: Static-Pedia: install it, configure it, write the wiki Source repository: https://github.com/evilsupervillain/staticpedia (branch master). Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/evilsupervillain/staticpedia/master/. Mental model The whole program is index.html. It is copied verbatim into a folder (the wiki root). Every .md file under that folder becomes a page. The page is chosen by the query string: no p → Index.md; ?p=Guides/Setup → Guides/Setup.md; ?p=Guides/ → Guides/Index.md. The .md is optional in p. In the browser, index.html fetches the .md, renders Markdown to HTML, sanitizes it, and rewrites links and media relative to the page's folder. There is no build step. The only generated file is the optional search index pages.json. Customization never requires editing index.html. Use staticpedia.json (config), style.css (CSS variables), _Sidebar.md and _Footer.md. Hard rules Do not modify index.html. Copy it byte-for-byte. All customization goes in the special files below. The only exception is the user explicitly asking for a new feature; then say so and keep the changes minimal. Home page is Index.md with a capital I. index.md does not work on case-sensitive hosts such as GitHub Pages and Linux servers, which are the common case. Use relative links only (rules in Links). Never write host-absolute URLs to your own pages and never hard-code the deploy path, such as /my-repo/. GitHub Pages needs an empty .nojekyll at the published root. Without it, _Sidebar.md and _Footer.md are not published and .md files with front matter get converted to HTML (every such page then 404s). Never invent facts. When documenting a project, derive every statement from its code, configs, README, issues or the user. Mark genuine unknowns with a > [!NOTE] callout instead of guessing. Verify before reporting done: run the link checker and the index generator, and serve the wiki once (see Verify). No third-party assets. No CDN scripts, no web fonts from Google Fonts or similar, no hot-linked images unless the user wants them. The wiki must work offline. Step 1: Decide the layout Pick the wiki root: Situation Wiki root Notes Project repo, docs alongside code (most common) docs/ GitHub Pages → Settings → Pages → Deploy from branch → /docs. Dedicated wiki/encyclopedia repo repo root Add README.md etc. to searchExclude. Site already has an index.html at the root a sub-folder, e.g. wiki/ Never overwrite an existing site's index.html. Existing folder of Markdown docs that folder Keep files; add index.html + Index.md; existing relative .md links keep working. SP=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/evilsupervillain/staticpedia/master mkdir -p "$WIKI" "$TOOLS" curl -fsSL "$SP/index.html" -o "$WIKI/index.html" curl -fsSL "$SP/tools/build-index.mjs" -o "$TOOLS/build-index.mjs" # pages.json generator (Node 18+) curl -fsSL "$SP/tools/check-links.mjs" -o "$TOOLS/check-links.mjs" # link/anchor checker (Node 18+) # optional, for machines without Node: curl -fsSL "$SP/tools/build_index.py" -o "$TOOLS/build_index.py" touch "$WIKI/.nojekyll" If raw downloads fail (network policy, private mirror), use git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/evilsupervillain/staticpedia /tmp/staticpedia and copy the same files. For reproducible installs, record the commit (git ls-remote https://github.com/evilsupervillain/staticpedia master) in the commit message. To upgrade later, replace index.html only. Sanity check: head -c 15 "$WIKI/index.html" prints and grep -c 'name="generator" content="Static-Pedia"' "$WIKI/index.html" prints 1. A failed download often saves an HTML error page instead. Index.md yes Home page. .nojekyll GitHub Pages only Empty file; disables Jekyll. staticpedia.json recommended Site name, logo, defaults. _Sidebar.md recommended Left navigation on every page. Links in it resolve from the wiki root. _Footer.md optional Footer on every page. Links resolve from the wiki root. style.css optional Loaded after built-in styles; override CSS variables here. pages.json optional (generated) Enables the search box, ?special=AllPages, ?special=Random. staticpedia.json Every key is optional.
